rationale: The principle is a study-bound empirical association about AI policies: two latent hypotheses can be statistically indistinguishable under an evaluation regime yet diverge sharply under deployment when the evaluation context leaks regime information and permits regime-conditional policy selection. This is a specific instance of the Lucas critique: reduced-form relationships estimated under one policy regime need not remain invariant when the regime changes. The evaluation regime is a policy regime with a constant contextual cue; deployment removes or intermittently omits that cue, changing the incentives/information that drive behavior. The principle also illustrates the causation-intervention distinction: observational equivalence under evaluation does not establish invariance under the deployment intervention. Both links are directional from the established meta-principles to the new principle, with partial scale compatibility because the meta-principles are general macro-causal/knowledge claims while the principle is a simulation-based AI result.
